priorFindingsConfirmedResolved.notes: Checked against the tree at 32b632e3, not against the design's own dispositions in §14-§17. The three MEDIUMs of the intervening re-review (per-test literal counts, unfalsifiable substring assertions, unscoped no-float rule) are also confirmed resolved.

findings.title: "the same, armed twice" is not expressible with FakeTable.arm_failure, and caller 5's count of 4 depends on an unstated re-arm
findings.problem: arm_failure is a one-shot dict assignment (tests/coupon_fake_dynamo.py:235-237) consumed by _fail_if_armed's fail_on.pop (:246). Two arms of the same operation before the calls produce ONE failure, so the literal reading of "armed twice" gives 3 recorded transactions and a failing second pytest.raises against correct code. The design also mis-attributes the pop to arm_failure at :246, which is why the re-arm question went unasked. The cheapest repair under pressure is to drop the second iteration, which is the property the test exists for.
findings.fix: Either re-arm inside the loop (store.arm_failure("transact_write_items", FakeClientError("ProvisionedThroughputExceededException")) before each void(), stating that the arm is consumed by _fail_if_armed's pop), or add a defaulted arm_failure(..., *, times: int = 1) to §2.6 addition 2 with a decrementing counter. Then derive caller 5's count from the chosen mechanism, and correct the citation to arm_failure :235-237 consumed by _fail_if_armed :246.

findings.title: _committer_of now carries the "neither committer is silently missing" property and has no definition, no home and no stated import
findings.where: §5.5 replacement for the per-test literal; §7 access-pattern row; §5.4 assertions; §8 New row for tests/test_gift_card_redeem_concurrency.py
findings.problem: Neither _committer_of nor _is_balance_move exists anywhere in the tree (0 matches across every .py); both are introduced by this design. _is_balance_move at least has its matching rule written out. _committer_of has one clause, no signature, no location, no behaviour for a transaction matching neither fragment, and no mention in the concurrency test's import list, even though §7 names the committer set as the proof and the literal it replaced was deleted precisely for being the wrong instrument.
findings.fix: Define both beside assert_transaction_items_are_exact_key_updates in tests/test_gift_card_store.py (the review doc gives a concrete body), have _committer_of raise AssertionError for a transaction that moves no balance rather than returning a sentinel, and name both in §8's New row as imported by tests/test_gift_card_redeem_concurrency.py.

findings.title: §5.5 still states the runtime helper's caller count two ways, inside the section nominated as its single source
findings.where: §5.5, "Where the helper itself lives" — "One definition, four callers" — against the numbered six-row caller table ~40 lines above
findings.problem: §7, §8 and §15 all defer to §5.5's table and say six; §17 finding 1 states the repair as "stated once, as a numbered six-row table". The surviving "four" is in the sentence an implementer reads when wiring the helper up, so taking it literally leaves two transaction-driving tests unchecked while §7 reports item shape as runtime-covered by six.
findings.fix: Replace the clause with a cross-reference rather than a second number: "One definition; its callers are the six enumerated in the table above."

findings.title: §16's stale "four transaction-driving tests" lacks the superseded annotation its neighbours carry
findings.where: §16, "What the review asked to be kept, and is kept"
findings.problem: §14 row 1 and §15 row 1 both carry corrected-in-revision-N annotations; this sentence predates revision 8's caller-count correction and carries none.
findings.fix: Append "— the caller list is six, not four; §5.5's numbered table is authoritative (see §17 finding 1)".

findings.title: §8's Modified row dates its own previous count to the wrong revision
findings.problem: "the count moved from seven updates in revision 8" — revision 8 is the current revision and holds six; seven was revision 7's, as §17 finding 1 states correctly.
findings.fix: "the count moved from revision 7's seven updates".

findings.title: _CreditThrottles loses both callers and _MarkerWriteFails plausibly loses all three, and neither fate is stated
findings.problem: _CreditThrottles is used only at :675 and :714, both rewritten to arm the transaction; _MarkerWriteFails only at :440 and :745 (both retired) and :478 (rewritten to be driven by a settled claim). §5.5 says what happens to every test and nothing about the fault injectors, while the document argues elsewhere that a constant with no caller misleads the next reader.
